## PCI PM callbacks that reach `i915_pm_suspend`

`i915_pm_suspend()` is itself a PCI PM callback, not a helper called by the other callbacks. The call chains are:

```text
PCI PM .suspend
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                         [i915_driver.c:1392]
     -> kdev_to_i915(kdev)
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                [i915_driver.c:1404]
        -> to_i915(dev)                            [i915_driver.c:1103]
        -> dev_priv->display
        -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)    [i915_driver.c:1120]
```

```text
PCI PM .poweroff
  -> i915_pm_suspend(kdev)                         [i915_driver.c:1745]
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)
        -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

The `.poweroff` callback is deliberately the same function as `.suspend`.

The hibernation freeze path also reaches the same suspend implementation, although it does **not** call `i915_pm_suspend()`:

```text
PCI PM .freeze
  -> i915_pm_freeze(kdev)                          [i915_driver.c:1483]
     -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                [i915_driver.c:1493]
        -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
     -> i915_gem_freeze(i915)
```

The switcheroo path is another non-`dev_pm_ops` caller:

```text
i915_driver_suspend_switcheroo(i915, state)         [i915_driver.c:1213]
  -> i915_drm_suspend(&i915->drm)                   [i915_driver.c:1223]
     -> intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
  -> i915_drm_suspend_late(&i915->drm, false)
  -> pci_save_state()
  -> pci_set_power_state(..., PCI_D3hot)
```

The PM table entries are:

```text
.prepare         = i915_pm_prepare
.suspend         = i915_pm_suspend
.suspend_late    = i915_pm_suspend_late
.suspend_noirq   = i915_pm_suspend_noirq
.freeze          = i915_pm_freeze
.poweroff        = i915_pm_suspend
.poweroff_late   = i915_pm_poweroff_late
.poweroff_noirq  = i915_pm_poweroff_noirq
.runtime_suspend = intel_runtime_suspend
```

Only `.suspend` and `.poweroff` invoke `i915_pm_suspend()` directly. `.freeze` independently invokes `i915_drm_suspend()`.

## Which of these callers also call runtime suspend?

None.

There is no `i915_pm_runtime_suspend` function in `drivers/gpu/drm/i915`. The separate runtime suspend path is:

```text
PCI/runtime PM .runtime_suspend
  -> intel_runtime_suspend(kdev)                   [i915_driver.c:1545]
     -> i915_gem_runtime_suspend(dev_priv)          [i915_driver.c:1566]
     -> intel_pxp_runtime_suspend(dev_priv->pxp)
     -> intel_gt_runtime_suspend(gt)
     -> intel_irq_suspend(dev_priv)
     -> intel_uncore_suspend(gt->uncore)
     -> intel_display_power_suspend(display)
     -> vlv_suspend_complete(dev_priv)
```

`intel_runtime_suspend()` does **not** call:

- `i915_pm_suspend()`
- `i915_drm_suspend()`
- `intel_display_driver_suspend()`

Thus, the system-suspend/display teardown path and runtime-suspend path are distinct.

## `dev_priv` data flow to display suspend

The data flow is:

```text
i915_pm_suspend(struct device *kdev)
  |
  | struct drm_i915_private *i915 = kdev_to_i915(kdev);
  |
  v
i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
  |
  | struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
  | struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
  |
  v
intel_display_driver_suspend(display)
```

At the call site in `i915_drm_suspend()`:

```c
static int i915_drm_suspend(struct drm_device *dev)
{
	struct drm_i915_private *dev_priv = to_i915(dev);
	struct intel_display *display = dev_priv->display;
	...
	intel_display_driver_suspend(display);
	...
}
```

`intel_display_driver_suspend()` is defined in:

- `linux/drivers/gpu/drm/i915/display/intel_display_driver.c:684`

Its own flow is:

